The '''54th Academy Awards''' ceremony, organized by the [[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] (AMPAS), honored [[1981 in film|films released in 1981]] and took place on March 29, 1982, at the [[Dorothy Chandler Pavilion]] in Los Angeles. During the ceremony, AMPAS presented [[Academy Awards]] (commonly referred to as Oscars) in 22 categories. The ceremony, televised in the United States by [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]], was produced by [[Howard W. Koch]] and directed by [[Marty Pasetta]].<ref>{{harvnb|Osborne|2013|p=413}}</ref> Comedian and talk show host [[Johnny Carson]] hosted the show for the fourth consecutive time.

''[[Chariots of Fire]]'' won four awards, including Best Picture.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Harmetz |first1=Aljean |author-link=Aljean Harmetz |title=Chariots of Fire, Katherine Hepburn and Henry Fonda win Top Oscars |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1982/03/30/movies/chariots-of-fire-katherine-hepburn-and-henry-fonda.html |access-date=March 24, 2022 |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=March 30, 1982 |archive-date=March 2, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230302221932/https://www.nytimes.com/1982/03/30/movies/chariots-of-fire-katherine-hepburn-and-henry-fonda.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Other winners included ''[[Raiders of the Lost Ark]]'' with also four awards,{{efn|name=Raiders}} ''[[On Golden Pond (1981 film)|On Golden Pond]]'' and ''[[Reds (film)|Reds]]'' with three, ''[[Arthur (1981 film)|Arthur]]'' with two; and ''[[An American Werewolf in London]]'', ''[[Close Harmony (1981 film)|Close Harmony]]'', ''[[Crac]]'', ''[[Genocide (1981 film)|Genocide]]'', ''[[Mephisto (1981 film)|Mephisto]]'', and ''[[Violet (1981 film)|Violet]]'' with one. The telecast garnered 46.2 million viewers in the United States.

The nominees for the 54th Academy Awards were announced on February 11, 1982, by Academy president [[Fay Kanin]] and actor [[Lloyd Bridges]].<ref>{{cite news |title=''On Golden Pond'' Top Oscar Contender |work=[[Boca Raton News]] |date=February 11, 1982}}</ref> ''[[Reds (film)|Reds]]'' earned the most nominations with twelve; ''[[On Golden Pond (1981 film)|On Golden Pond]]'' came in second with ten.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Tuck |first1=Lon |title=And the Nominees Are... |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/lifestyle/1982/02/12/and-the-nominees-are/d9cfcbc4-8606-42b2-8e30-1693369970cd/ |access-date=March 24, 2022 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=February 12, 1982}}</ref>  The winners were announced at the awards ceremony on March 29.

Best Director winner [[Warren Beatty]] became the first person to earn acting, directing, producing, and screenwriting nominations for the same film for the second time. He previously earned nominations in the same categories for 1978's ''[[Heaven Can Wait (1978 film)|Heaven Can Wait]]''.<ref>{{harvnb|Wiley|Bona|1996|p=1138}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Emerson |first1=Jim |title=Questions for the Academy |url=https://www.rogerebert.com/scanners/questions-for-the-academy |access-date=March 21, 2016 |work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]] |date=February 11, 2007 |archive-date=March 13, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170313185720/http://www.rogerebert.com/scanners/questions-for-the-academy |url-status=live }}</ref> ''On Golden Pond'' was the fifth film to win both lead acting awards.<ref name="Osborne 2013 423">{{harvnb|Osborne|2013|p=423}}</ref> Best Actress winner [[Katharine Hepburn]] became the first and only performer to win four competitive acting Oscars.<ref>{{harvnb|Holden|1993|p=608}}</ref> Furthermore, the 48-year span between her first win for 1933's ''[[Morning Glory (1933 film)|Morning Glory]]'' and her last win for ''On Golden Pond'' set the record for the longest span between first and last career Oscar wins.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Davis |first1=Clayton |title=In Celebration of Katharine Hepburn's Birthday, Here Are 12 Actors Who Should Also Have Four Oscar Wins |url=https://variety.com/lists/four-oscars-winners-katharine-hepburn-meryl-streep-kate-winslet-denzel-washington-al-pacino/ |access-date=March 24, 2022 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=May 12, 2021 |archive-date=August 20, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220820025435/https://variety.com/lists/four-oscars-winners-katharine-hepburn-meryl-streep-kate-winslet-denzel-washington-al-pacino/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award===
The award recognizes individuals whose humanitarian efforts have brought credit to the motion picture industry.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award |url=https://www.oscars.org/governors/hersholt |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |access-date=12 November 2020 |archive-date=16 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201116224625/https://www.oscars.org/governors/hersholt |url-status=live }}</ref>

* [[Danny Kaye]]<ref name="Winners search" />

===Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award===
The award honors "creative producers whose bodies of work reflect a consistently high quality of motion picture production".<ref>{{cite news|title=Irvin G. Thalberg Memorial Award |url=http://www.oscars.org/governors/thalberg |access-date=December 18, 2015 |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160101224449/http://oscars.org/governors/thalberg |archive-date=January 1, 2016 }}</ref>

* [[Albert R. Broccoli]]<ref name="Winners search" />

==Ceremony information==
[[File:Johnny Carson 1970.JPG|thumb|left|alt=Johnny Carson in 1970|[[Johnny Carson]] hosted the 54th Academy Awards.]]
In November 1981, the Academy hired film director, screenwriter, and producer [[Melvin Frank]] to produce the telecast for the first time. "The Academy is fortunate that Melvin Frank has agreed to make himself available for our show," said AMPAS President [[Fay Kanin]] in a press release announcing the selection. "He joins a distinguished list of producers who have consistently made the Academy Awards the entertainment highlight of the year."<ref>{{cite web |title=Melvin Frank to Produce 54th Oscar Show |url=https://digitalcollections.oscars.org/digital/collection/p15759coll9/id/7474/rec/8 |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |access-date=October 11, 2021 |date=November 16, 1981 |archive-date=October 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221005080631/https://digitalcollections.oscars.org/digital/collection/p15759coll9/id/7474/rec/8 |url-status=live }}</ref> Two months later, it was announced that comedian and ''[[The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson|The Tonight Show]]'' host [[Johnny Carson]] would preside over emceeing duties for the 1982 ceremony.<ref>{{cite press release |last=Morgan |first=Don |title=Johnny Carson to Serves As Master of Ceremonies for 54th Annual Academy Awards |url=https://digitalcollections.oscars.org/digital/collection/p15759coll9/id/7481/rec/8 |access-date=January 10, 2022 |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |date=January 12, 1982 |archive-date=October 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221005083417/https://digitalcollections.oscars.org/digital/collection/p15759coll9/id/7481/rec/8 |url-status=live }}</ref> In February 1982, [[Howard W. Koch]] took over producing duties after Frank had been hospitalized for complications stemming from a virus.<ref name="Frank" /> Koch stated that all artistic contributions made by Frank would remain during the production of the festivities.<ref>{{cite web |title=Howard W. Koch to Take Over Production of Academy Awards Show |url=https://digitalcollections.oscars.org/digital/collection/p15759coll9/id/7499/rec/8 |access-date=October 11, 2021 |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]] |date=February 19, 1982 |archive-date=October 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221005082636/https://digitalcollections.oscars.org/digital/collection/p15759coll9/id/7499/rec/8 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Introduction of Best Makeup award===
Beginning with this ceremony, AMPAS introduced a new competitive award that would honor achievement in makeup.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://latimes.newspapers.com/newspage/389006882/ |access-date=April 10, 2026 |title=New Makeup Category Set Up for Academy Awards |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=December 24, 1981 |page=47}}{{subscription required}}</ref> According to Academy executive administrator John Pavlik, the category would be presented if a special committee composed of makeup artists, hairstylists, cinematographers, and other related craftspeople determined that at least one film was deemed worthy of such awards. Members would be able to nominate up to five films, and the committee would review the seven films receiving the most votes to select up to three nominees.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Arar |first1=Yardena |title=Makeup Artists to Get Oscar Category |work=[[Oakland Tribune]] |date=December 18, 1981 |page=C-4}}</ref> Prior to the introduction of this category, 1964's ''[[7 Faces of Dr. Lao]]'' and 1968's ''[[Planet of the Apes (1968 film)|Planet of the Apes]]'' were given special honorary awards.<ref>{{cite news |title=Motion Picture Academy to Honnor Makeup Artists |work=[[Santa Cruz Sentinel]] |date=December 18, 1981 |page=29}}</ref>

===Critical reviews===
''[[Tampa Bay Times|St. Petersburg Times]]'' film critic Thomas Sabulis wrote, "The Academy Awards show was a reasonably good television product. The acceptance speeches were thankfully brief and concise."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sabulis |first1=Thomas |title=Oscar Strikes a Balance in Honoring 1981 Films |work=[[Tampa Bay Times|St. Petersburg Times]] |date=March 31, 1982 |page=2D}}</ref> Columnist [[Janet Maslin]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' remarked, "Thanks largely to the fancifulness of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences' voters, Monday night's Oscar presentation was the most exciting in recent years. When the awards show itself is something less than swift or glamorous, which was certainly the case this year, it can still come to life if the voting takes a sufficiently strange turn."<ref name="Maslin" /> ''[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|The Atlanta Constitution]]'' critic Scott Cain commented, "The academy has steadily increased the amount of showpieces. These musical numbers worked splendidly this year and the program was relatively painless at 3.5 hours in length."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Cain |first1=Scott |title=Oscar Strikes a Balance in Honoring 1981 Films |work=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution|The Atlanta Constitution]] |page=2-H}}</ref>

[[Harold Schindler]] of ''[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]'' called the ceremony "a three-and-a-half-hour marathon which sparkled in spots, sputtered in others, and featured some of the most uneven casting in the program's history."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Schindler |first1=Harold |title=Oscar Night Was a Drawn-Out Marathon |work=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]] |date=March 31, 1982 |page=C5}}</ref> ''[[Austin American-Statesman]]'' film critic Patrick Taggart quipped, "Whether or not the awards will be taken more seriously in the future, the ceremony last Monday night certainly had the dreariness one associates with serious events."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Taggart |first1=Patrick |title=New Credibility |work=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |date=April 4, 1982 |page=179}}</ref> ''[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]'' columnist Desmond Ryan commented that due to many winners being absent from the festivities, "An already dull evening lapsed into long stretches of tedium."<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ryan |first1=Desmond |title=The Swift, The Old Shine with Oscar |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=March 31, 1982 |page=5D}}</ref>

===Ratings and reception===
The American telecast on ABC drew in an average of 46.2 million people over the length of the entire ceremony.<ref name="Viewership">{{cite news|title=Top-10 Most Watched Academy Awards Broadcasts |url=https://www.nielsen.com/insights/2009/top-10-most-watched-academy-awards-broadcasts/ |publisher=[[Nielsen N.V.]] |date=February 18, 2009 |access-date=August 25, 2015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160127130438/http://www.nielsen.com/us/en/insights/news/2009/top-10-most-watched-academy-awards-broadcasts.html |archive-date=January 27, 2016 }}</ref> Moreover, the show drew higher [[Nielsen Media Research|Nielsen ratings]] compared to the previous ceremony, with 33.6% of households watching with a 53% share.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Holston |first1=Noel |title=ABC Takes Ratings Top Stop with Some Help From Oscar |work=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |date=April 10, 1982 |page=B10}}</ref>

In August 1982, the ceremony presentation received three nominations at the [[34th Primetime Emmy Awards|34th Primetime Emmys]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Margulies |first1=Lee |title=Emmy Award Nominations: The Peacock Shows its Colors |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=August 6, 1982 |pages=101, 104}}</ref> The following month, it won an award for Ray Klausen's [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Production Design for a Variety, Reality or Competition Series|art direction]] of the program.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Fifty-Fourth Annual Academy Awards |url=https://www.emmys.com/shows/fifty-fourth-annual-academy-awards |publisher=Academy of Television Arts and Sciences |access-date=September 12, 2022 |archive-date=September 25, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220925102901/https://www.emmys.com/shows/fifty-fourth-annual-academy-awards |url-status=live }}</ref>
